v.rationale:
I rank impl-1 first, impl-2 second and impl-3 third. All three test suites pass: impl-1 37/37, impl-2 31/31, impl-3 37/37. All three use the same core pattern: createOrFirst on a unique event_id, WithoutOverlapping keyed by the event, RateLimited with perSecond(10), backoff and MaxExceptions attributes, failed() recording the error, MassPrunable plus a scheduled model:prune, and a policy-gated FormRequest index.

impl-1 is the most complete:
- Conditional-UPDATE state transitions make processing idempotent and safe when events arrive out of order. The receipt goes out only on a real transition.
- retryUntil stops middleware releases from using up the retry budget, and 429 responses use Retry-After.
- A recovery command picks up events whose dispatch was lost or whose worker died.
- It has the best production README and the strongest tests, which run a real database worker and check exact backoff delays, the rate limit and the lock.
- Its bugs are minor. A missing payment_id throws an ErrorException and retries instead of failing cleanly. A malformed payload sent without Accept: application/json gets a 302 redirect because the route is in the web group.

impl-2 is lean and idiomatic:
- It has its own webhooks routes file without session middleware, and every bad-input case fails cleanly.
- `queue:retry` works on failed events.
- Its tests also use a real worker.
- But OrderFactory leaves out the required user_id, so `Order::factory()->create()` fails.
- Order status updates are unconditional, so late events can move a refunded order back to payment_failed and then to paid, with a second receipt (probe confirmed).

impl-3 comes last:
- It has the same state-regression problem as impl-2.
- A fixed Tries(30) budget is also used up by rate-limit and overlap releases, so healthy events can fail under load.
- Its README recommends `queue:retry`, but the job skips Failed events, so a retry does nothing (probe confirmed).
- The refunds table is created inside the orders migration, and the payload stores the whole envelope.
- Its tests are the weakest: they check attributes by reflection, use mocked jobs for the middleware, and never run a real worker through backoff.
